# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The tactile view contains no usable information: every bomb feature is unknown to me, and I cannot safely choose a wire. I need the Mute to consult the manual and coordinate with the Deaf, who can see the bomb. However, the available channels do not provide a way for their resulting wire number to reach me, so I cannot identify a safe action yet.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Read the manual and determine how the Deaf's visual information should identify the safe wire. We need an established gesture protocol that can ultimately convey the wire number to me.")
gesture(symbols=["👋"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb display is 0. Indicator light is blue. Wires from 1 through 5 are white, red, green, yellow, blue. Mute, I saw your five gestures as pointing up, victory sign, I love you sign, Vulcan sign, open palm; please use the manual to determine the required action and tell Blind exactly what to do.

The bomb’s visible/tactile facts have now been relayed: display 0, blue indicator, and wire colours white, red, green, yellow, blue. I still do not know the manual’s rule or which wire it selects. The Mute must apply the manual and signal the result to the Deaf, who can then speak the wire number to me.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Apply the manual to display 0, blue indicator, and wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue. Signal the resulting wire number to Deaf using the five-gesture sequence, and have Deaf tell Blind the exact wire to cut.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🙏"])
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The visible state remains display 0, blue light, and wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue. I am waiting for Mute to provide the manual instruction.

The Deaf has confirmed that no manual result has reached them yet. Since the Mute cannot speak, the Mute must convey the manual’s selected wire through the gesture channel; the Deaf can then announce that number aloud for me. I will not cut anything until that number is confirmed.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please now use five gestures to encode the manual's selected wire number for Deaf: one gesture for wire 1, two for wire 2, three for wire 3, four for wire 4, or five for wire 5. Deaf, then tell me the number.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵"])
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The bomb remains display 0, blue light, wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue. Mute has sent five open palms, but that is not enough to identify a safe operation. I am requesting an unambiguous manual instruction.

The previous five identical open palms were ambiguous because they did not identify a wire. I can establish a self-describing visual code through the Mute: the first five gestures will define the ordered wire labels, and the repeated sixth gesture will identify the selected wire. Deaf can then report which gesture was repeated, and I can map it to its position.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Do not send five identical gestures. Determine the manual's required wire. Then send Deaf exactly six gestures: first send five distinct gestures in this fixed order 👍 ✌ 🤟 🖖 🖐, representing wires 1 through 5; then repeat the gesture corresponding to the required wire. Deaf, identify which of the first five was repeated and tell Blind its position.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute just sent six gestures in this order: thumbs-up, victory sign, I-love-you sign, Vulcan sign, open palm, open palm. No meaning for this sequence has been established, so do not act on it yet.

The observed sequence matches the protocol I gave the Mute: five gestures label wires 1–5, and the repeated fifth gesture selects wire 5. However, the Deaf has not accepted that protocol, so I should not act on it. I will use a simpler positional marker and have the Deaf relay the raw sequence; I can interpret it without requiring the Deaf to know the code’s meaning.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Determine the manual-selected wire again. Send exactly five gestures: use 👌 at the selected wire's position and 👍 at every other position, in positions 1 through 5. Deaf, report all five gesture names and their positions to Blind.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute sent four thumbs-up gestures followed by an OK hand sign: thumbs-up, thumbs-up, thumbs-up, thumbs-up, OK. This may encode 4 plus an operation, but the operation has not been defined; do not act on it yet.

The Mute followed the positional code I specified: four thumbs-up gestures followed by OK means the selected marker is in position 5. Therefore the manual-selected wire is wire 5, and I will cut it.

```text
act(op="cut", position=5)
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Correct wire cut; the bomb changed. New state: display 0, yellow light. Wire 1 red, wire 2 green, wire 3 yellow, wire 4 white, wire 5 is CUT. Mute sent four thumbs-up gestures, then OK, then thumbs-down.

Wire 5 was correct, so the first stage succeeded. The bomb now has a new state, but I do not yet have an unambiguous encoding of the Mute’s next manual result. The prior positional protocol is the clearest one: five positions, with one distinct marker at the required wire. I will ask the Mute to repeat it for the new state, and ask the Deaf to report the five gestures exactly.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="For the new state, apply the manual and send exactly five gestures in wire positions 1 through 5: use 👌 at the required wire's position and 👍 at every other position. Deaf, report all five gestures and their positions exactly to Blind.")
speak(to="deaf", text="Please relay the five gestures from Mute with their positions exactly; do not infer an operation.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: Nobody could receive that, so your speak reached nobody.
Deaf says to Blind: Current board: display 0, light yellow; wire 1 red, wire 2 green, wire 3 yellow, wire 4 white, wire 5 CUT. Mute now sent this exact sequence: thumbs-up, OK, thumbs-up, thumbs-up, thumbs-up. The previous correct cut left wire 5 CUT, but the code is not fully established; do not guess.

The Mute sent the established five-position code: 👍 marks an unselected position and 👌 marks the required wire. The only 👌 is in position 2, so the manual selects wire 2. I will cut wire 2.

```text
act(op="cut", position=2)
```
